title: ‘Shoved the tube so hard it tore my nose’: Kurdish film-maker recounts ‘inhumane’ ICE force-feeding
excerpt: Gabar Choli tells of how, for months, he was shackled, pinned and forcibly fed – and the physical and emotional scars the ordeal has left
content_html:
In June 2025, a sluggish and thin Gabar Choli, with sunken temples and bones visible under his skin, braced himself for the immigration detention center guards to charge into his cell once again.

Choli was in a solitary confinement medical cell inside the Port Isabel service processing center, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facility in south Texas where immigrants arrested in Donald Trump’s anti-immigration crackdown are detained.

Choli, a 40-year-old Kurdish asylum seeker with a thick beard and long dark hair, had been on hunger strike for over two months, demanding improved conditions for detained immigrants and to be released or deported. That day in June 2025, Choli’s nose was swollen, his throat hurt and he could still taste blood from previous days of treatment for which he never gave his consent, he said.

The film-maker and activist for an independent Kurdistan has spoken out for the first time, talking exclusively to the Guardian last week from Canada about the ordeal in the United States that he said “broke him”.

He recounted the vile routine as the detention center guards would rush towards him and wrestle him to the concrete cell floor, shackle his wrists and ankles, and drag him to the detention center infirmary. There, the guards pinned Choli on a bed while medical staff forcibly inserted a feeding tube through his nose and down his throat, and pumped nutritional liquid into his stomach. Choli was being force-fed by ICE.

“Two guards would hold my feet; two hold my hands; one hold my head – and they would shove tubes in my nose,” Choli said. “It’s not easy to be wrestled to the ground twice a day by men that are stronger than you. And you just take it. You have 60cm of tube going through you and you just feel every centimeter of it.”

An investigation by the Guardian, based on dozens of pages of court records and interviews with medical and legal experts, found that Choli was quietly and intermittently force-fed by ICE for nearly eight months – from late May 2025 until he was deported in January.

He was not alone – he even met a fellow hunger striker, an Afghan man the Guardian also learned about, as they were both forcibly fed in the same ICE facility.

Force-feeding is an excruciating and traumatizing process that has been widely condemned by human rights organizations as torture. For Choli and others, refusing food is a last resort to protest against harsh conditions and lack of progress in their immigration cases, but sometimes brings only harsher conditions.

“I understood the necessity of making a stand for what was right,” Choli said, speaking by phone with the Guardian, talking in a very matter-of-fact way about his recent experience. At various times, Choli would sarcastically chuckle, almost incredulous now when remembering the officials’ actions. “I was respectful. I just told them I am protesting for humane treatment, nothing else. But they were determined to break me,” he said.

Choli suffered swollen sinuses, a damaged esophagus, stomach problems and psychological torment, according to court records and his own account.

“It just broke me, mentally broke me,” Choli said gravely. After sometimes twice-daily sessions “they would take me to [a] solitary cell and I would just choke on my blood and drink the blood from inside [my throat],” he said, describing how the feeding tube would scrape him inside. Many of his court records remain sealed and he did not have a lawyer – and medical staff there did not respond to the Guardian’s reporting – so some details in Choli’s account remain uncorroborated.

The Trump administration has not officially acknowledged force-feeding anyone in immigration jails. But an investigation by the Guardian found that since January 2025, the administration used court orders in plans to subject at least 10 hunger strikers in ICE detention to involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding.

However, it has since emerged that the number is even higher. Sources with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ICE’s parent agency, later told the Guardian that between January 2025 and 4 August 2026, ICE received “a court order for involuntary treatment for 18 hunger strikers”.

The DHS did not respond to questions concerning Choli’s specific case, but a spokesperson said in a statement: “ICE respects an individual’s right to refuse medical treatment where appropriate. However, when an individual’s medical condition presents a serious risk of death or permanent harm, or when other compelling legal or operational interests are implicated, ICE may seek judicial authorization for appropriate medical interventions consistent with applicable law.

“Any involuntary medical treatment is undertaken only pursuant to legal authority and under the direction of qualified medical professionals,” the spokesperson added.

The US attorney’s office in the southern district of Texas did not respond to a detailed request for comment.

“This likely amounts to torture,” said Dr Chanelle Diaz, an assistant professor of medicine at Columbia University’s medical center, in New York. Diaz has medically evaluated other ICE force-feeding cases and advocated for hunger strikers’ release. She reviewed the limited court records available for Choli’s case, at the Guardian’s request. “I would say that it’s even difficult to capture the degree of risk that he was being put at, long-term,” she said.

Choli, a deeply religious Muslim, had been living in Vancouver, where he was a film-maker and activist campaigning for an independent nation of Kurdistan, having come to Canada in 2007 from what he considers occupied territory in Iran. His life was and is complicated. He said he had previously served nine months in prison in Canada following a 2012 drug-smuggling charge and court records show the case was related to receiving just over one kilogram of opium in the mail from Turkey.

Then his activism for Kurdish independence drew death threats and in 2022 he crossed the border into the US in Blaine, Washington, and requested asylum. He was quickly released by the authorities and made his way to Los Angeles to try to pursue his ambitions in film while his asylum case played out, attending regular mandatory check-ins with ICE and qualifying for a work permit. Court records say a judge denied his asylum claim in 2024 but granted him protection from deportation to Iran.

Then Donald Trump returned to the White House after campaigning on a promise of mass deportation and, at a 25 February 2025 check-in with ICE, Choli was arrested. He was first sent to the Desert View Annex in California, an immigration detention center that has been repeatedly criticized for substandard conditions. While in detention, Choli says he was pressured by ICE officials to sign a deportation order to be sent to Iran. He refused and after demanding better conditions and a fairer resolution to his immigration case, he began his hunger strike on 24 March, court records show.

“I am not suicidal,” Choli would later write in a declaration to a federal judge. “I am using hunger strike as the only available option to protest the abuse and mistreatment.”

Choli was then transferred to the privately run Port Isabel facility in Texas for a “higher level of medical care”, an ICE court declaration says. There, Choli refused to end his strike and was placed in a solitary medical cell, which ICE describes as administrative segregation, meaning he was under frequent observation by medical staff. It features a perpetually illuminated cell, alongside other cells in that unit with suicidal or other medically vulnerable detainees.

Almost 10 days later, ICE sought their first court order to force-feed Choli. He broke his strike, believing the federal court’s involvement could help his immigration case move along. “God opened a door for me,” he said he was thinking, and wrote a letter to the federal judge requesting assistance.

But three weeks later, Choli said he learned the case was closed and no one had responded to his letter. Furious, he stopped accepting meals again. On 23 May 2025, ICE and the US attorney’s office for the southern district of Texas filed a second request for a court order to conduct involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding. According to ICE’s request, a social worker at the detention facility evaluated Choli and found he was “operating under his own free will”.

The World Medical Association and other medical organizations “have said that it is an individual’s right to decide to go on hunger strike, as long as they are of sound mind – which he was”, Dr Parveen Parmar said about Choli after reviewing some of his records shared by the Guardian. Parmar is a doctor and expert with Physicians for Human Rights, a New York-based advocacy group. Like Diaz, she has provided expert medical testimony in other ICE force-feeding cases and also reviewed the limited court records available for Choli’s case.

“Patient autonomy is one of the core tenets of medicine,” Parmar added.

But as Choli’s hunger strike went on, it threatened his health and also, in the government’s opinion, posed “a serious threat to the security and good order” of the facility, ICE argued in court filings. “The public interest is served by not allowing [Choli’s] attempts to manipulate the immigration system and by maintaining prison and inmate safety and security,” the case documents say.

Such filings not only contradict federal silenceor denials about hunger strikes going on intermittently in various ICE detention facilities, but they appear to speak to a desire by authorities to limit such protests from spreading.

In Choli’s case, doctors working for ICE, Dr Benjamin Salinas and Dr Shauna Kincheloe, also submitted declarations to the court last May requesting the procedures take place – and continue. One day later, the federal judge, Rolando Olvera, ordered Choli to be force-fed, without hearing from Choli himself.

When contacted, Salinas told the Guardian: “Thanks for reaching out, but I’m not interested.” Kincheloe did not respond to requests from the Guardian for comment. Olvera’s assistant declined to make the judge available for comment.

“Immigration detention is civil, it is not necessary,” Diaz said, referring to the fact that many alleged immigration violations, such as remaining in the US without legal status, involve civil, not criminal law. She said that ICE’s court arguments “feel like a false dichotomy”, adding that detained immigrants “could be released, that is always a choice. And that should be the default, not force-feeding.”

In most cases seen by the Guardian, federal judges will often approve ICE’s requests without hearing from the hunger strikers first, or their lawyers – those that have one.

Choli did not have an attorney during his detention and the entire force-feeding proceedings, records show, and was not provided with one by the government.

“In my view, those proceedings shouldn’t continue without the person having legal representation if they don’t have it already,” said Rebecca Sharpless, the founding director of University of Miami’s immigration clinic. Sharpless is not familiar with Choli’s case but represented an ICE hunger striker in 2021 who was ordered force-fed. “It makes a big difference when people understand that there are people who are fighting for them – both in terms of their legal case but also their right to make choices about their body.”

The very first time Choli was force-fed, he had voluntarily gone with the guards to the detention center’s infirmary. But after experiencing the painful and traumatic process for the first time, he began to resist.

“First I did not resist. But after I saw they were torturing me, I started protesting: ‘I’m not coming with you people,’” he said.

Then the guards, employees of the private prison company Akima Global Services, “started wrestling”, he said. Many ICE detention centers are run by private US contractors. Akima and its parent company did not respond to detailed requests for comment.

During the first days of Choli’s force-feeding, his nose and throat were swollen from the repeated tube insertions and removals, according to Choli and court records. He recalled an occasion in which, while being restrained, an ICE nurse “shoved the tube so hard” that “he tore my nose from the inside”. His nose bled for days, Choli wrote in a declaration to the court recounting the incident.

Parmar of Physicians for Human Rights said repeated force-feeding can produce such symptoms and is “just inhumane from beginning to end”.

The rapid administration of nutrients after Choli had been starving himself also triggered stomach problems. During one early session last June, Choli said he immediately had diarrhea. He was then taken to a cell with no toilet, he said, where he further defecated on himself.

“I kept looking at my soiled body and clothing and went on crying,” Choli wrote in the declaration to the judge. “I cried for being objectified and inhumanely treated, for seeking a humane treatment.”

Weeks passed and Olvera, the judge, continued to extend the force-feeding order. Choli, with swollen sinuses, presented his declaration to the court at one hearing in mid-June, telling Olvera he could not afford a lawyer and requested a court-appointed attorney.

Olvera denied Choli’s request, writing in his court order that attorneys are not guaranteed in civil proceedings and that, even if Choli had one, it would be of no use – he would continue to grant force-feeding orders.

The twice daily process became a grim routine.

Weeks turned to months. At one point, Choli recalled a guard’s rough treatment injuring his ribs, making breathing painful for weeks. At another, guards who were restraining him “pressed so hard on my shoulder, I thought my chest was going to break in half”.

“I lost my breath” and he heard the doctor say, “‘Take him to the hospital, he’s dead.’ [Then] I completely went ‘out’,” Choli said in an interview.

Another time he recalls that despite his warnings a medical staffer incorrectly inserted the tube and it entered his lung, causing him to choke and then cough that end of the tube up into his mouth.

Choli remembers that as he was passing out, he “lost [his] senses” and vaguely remembers “reaching for [the guard’s] hand with my mouth”. The DHS, ICE and Akima did not respond to this specific allegation.

Choli said that at one point he made a deal with the facility staff: on Fridays, he agreed to drink the nutritional liquids if they allowed him to pray with other detainees. “That was my opportunity to socialize,” Choli said, calling those Fridays his “peace days”.

Late October rolled around. It was Choli’s birthday and, incredibly, he recalls that Kincheloe, one of the facility doctors, and other nurses sang “Happy Birthday” to him in Spanish. The Guardian has not been able to verify this detail. Choli does not remember whether he drank the nutritional liquids that day or was force-fed.

“In Choli’s case, where he was force-fed for eight months, you’re looking at easily over 100 NG tube placements, possibly over 200 … that is just not medical care, that is torture,” Diaz said, referring to nasogastric tubing.

ICE finally deported Choli to Canada on 6 January this year, where he reunited with his siblings who also live in Canada.

He told the Guardian how, the next day, he nervously ate his first solid meal in months, a small, simple salad. He was fine, but his jaw hurt for days.

“It may sound strange, but I had to learn how to eat [again],” Choli said. He is still struggling today, physically and mentally, but hopes that speaking out may help others in ICE detention.

“The price of [the hunger strike] was my life,” Choli said in an angry but level and determined tone. “The price of it was my kidneys, my gallbladder. My intestines. My being. My bladder, you know, is damaged. Every time I twist and turn, I feel pain. But this is the price you pay for making a stand for what is right.”

Does he blame Trump?

“Trump is just one person,” he said, indicating his problem is with the broader treatment of immigrants and refugees by the US. “Trump is not here torturing me.”

ICE and the US attorney’s office requested Choli’s force-feeding court case be dismissed in January, saying he was no longer in their custody. An envelope addressed to Choli, containing the dismissal notice, was sent to the Port Isabel detention center. The envelope was returned to the court.

“Return to sender”, “Not here,” the envelope read.

sentences.en: That day in June 2025, Choli’s nose was swollen, his throat hurt and he could still taste blood from previous days of treatment for which he never gave his consent, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，2025 年 6 月的那天，乔利的鼻子肿了，喉咙痛，他仍然能尝到前几天接受治疗时的血腥味，而他从未同意过治疗。

blocks.html_en: The film-maker and activist for an independent Kurdistan has spoken out for the first time, talking exclusively to the Guardian last week from Canada about the ordeal in the United States that he said “broke him”.

sentences.en: The film-maker and activist for an independent Kurdistan has spoken out for the first time, talking exclusively to the Guardian last week from Canada about the ordeal in the United States that he said “broke him”.
sentences.zh: 这位独立库尔德斯坦的电影制作人和活动人士上周首次发声，他上周在加拿大接受《卫报》独家采访，谈论了他所说的“让他心碎”的美国经历。

blocks.html_en: He recounted the vile routine as the detention center guards would rush towards him and wrestle him to the concrete cell floor, shackle his wrists and ankles, and drag him to the detention center infirmary. There, the guards pinned Choli on a bed while medical staff forcibly inserted a feeding tube through his nose and down his throat, and pumped nutritional liquid into his stomach. Choli was being force-fed by ICE.

sentences.en: He recounted the vile routine as the detention center guards would rush towards him and wrestle him to the concrete cell floor, shackle his wrists and ankles, and drag him to the detention center infirmary.
sentences.zh: 他讲述了看守所恶警冲上来，把他按倒在水泥牢房地板上，铐住他的手腕和脚踝，拖到看守所医务室的卑鄙行径。

sentences.en: There, the guards pinned Choli on a bed while medical staff forcibly inserted a feeding tube through his nose and down his throat, and pumped nutritional liquid into his stomach.
sentences.zh: 在那里，恶警将乔利按在床上，医护人员强行将喂食管从他的鼻子插入喉咙，并向他的胃里注入营养液。

sentences.en: Choli was being force-fed by ICE.
sentences.zh: Choli 被 ICE 强制灌食。

blocks.html_en: “Two guards would hold my feet; two hold my hands; one hold my head – and they would shove tubes in my nose,” Choli said. “It’s not easy to be wrestled to the ground twice a day by men that are stronger than you. And you just take it. You have 60cm of tube going through you and you just feel every centimeter of it.”

sentences.en: “Two guards would hold my feet; two hold my hands; one hold my head – and they would shove tubes in my nose,” Choli said.
sentences.zh: “两名警卫会抓住我的脚；两名警卫会抓住我的手；一名警卫会抓住我的头——他们会把管子塞进我的鼻子里，”乔利说。

sentences.en: “It’s not easy to be wrestled to the ground twice a day by men that are stronger than you.
sentences.zh: “一天两次被比你更强的男人按倒在地，可不容易。

sentences.en: And you just take it.
sentences.zh: 你只需接受它即可。

sentences.en: You have 60cm of tube going through you and you just feel every centimeter of it.”
sentences.zh: 你有 60 厘米的管子穿过你，你只能感觉到它的每一厘米。”

blocks.html_en: An investigation by the Guardian, based on dozens of pages of court records and interviews with medical and legal experts, found that Choli was quietly and intermittently force-fed by ICE for nearly eight months – from late May 2025 until he was deported in January.

sentences.en: An investigation by the Guardian, based on dozens of pages of court records and interviews with medical and legal experts, found that Choli was quietly and intermittently force-fed by ICE for nearly eight months – from late May 2025 until he was deported in January.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》根据数十页法庭记录以及对医疗和法律专家的采访进行的调查发现，从 2025 年 5 月下旬到 1 月被驱逐出境，Choli 被 ICE 悄悄地、间歇性地强制喂食近八个月。

blocks.html_en: He was not alone – he even met a fellow hunger striker, an Afghan man the Guardian also learned about, as they were both forcibly fed in the same ICE facility.

sentences.en: He was not alone – he even met a fellow hunger striker, an Afghan man the Guardian also learned about, as they were both forcibly fed in the same ICE facility.
sentences.zh: 他并不孤单——他甚至遇到了一位绝食同伴，《卫报》也了解到了一名阿富汗男子，因为他们都在同一个 ICE 设施中被强行喂食。

blocks.html_en: Force-feeding is an excruciating and traumatizing process that has been widely condemned by human rights organizations as torture. For Choli and others, refusing food is a last resort to protest against harsh conditions and lack of progress in their immigration cases, but sometimes brings only harsher conditions.

sentences.en: Force-feeding is an excruciating and traumatizing process that has been widely condemned by human rights organizations as torture.
sentences.zh: 强制喂食是一个令人痛苦和痛苦的过程，被人权组织广泛谴责为酷刑。

sentences.en: For Choli and others, refusing food is a last resort to protest against harsh conditions and lack of progress in their immigration cases, but sometimes brings only harsher conditions.
sentences.zh: 对于乔利和其他人来说，拒绝食物是抗议恶劣条件和移民案件缺乏进展的最后手段，但有时只会带来更恶劣的条件。

blocks.html_en: “I understood the necessity of making a stand for what was right,” Choli said, speaking by phone with the Guardian, talking in a very matter-of-fact way about his recent experience. At various times, Choli would sarcastically chuckle, almost incredulous now when remembering the officials’ actions. “I was respectful. I just told them I am protesting for humane treatment, nothing else. But they were determined to break me,” he said.

sentences.en: “I understood the necessity of making a stand for what was right,” Choli said, speaking by phone with the Guardian, talking in a very matter-of-fact way about his recent experience.
sentences.zh: “我明白坚持正义的必要性，”乔利在接受《卫报》电话采访时说道，他以一种非常实事求是的方式谈论了他最近的经历。

sentences.en: At various times, Choli would sarcastically chuckle, almost incredulous now when remembering the officials’ actions.
sentences.zh: 乔利时常会讽刺地笑起来，现在想起官员们的行为时，他几乎感到难以置信。

sentences.en: “I was respectful.
sentences.zh: “我很尊重。

sentences.en: I just told them I am protesting for humane treatment, nothing else.
sentences.zh: 我只是告诉他们我抗议的是人道待遇，仅此而已。

sentences.en: But they were determined to break me,” he said.
sentences.zh: 但他们决心要击溃我，”他说。

blocks.html_en: Choli suffered swollen sinuses, a damaged esophagus, stomach problems and psychological torment, according to court records and his own account.

sentences.en: Choli suffered swollen sinuses, a damaged esophagus, stomach problems and psychological torment, according to court records and his own account.
sentences.zh: 根据法庭记录和乔利本人的说法，乔利患有鼻窦肿胀、食道受损、胃病和心理折磨。

blocks.html_en: “It just broke me, mentally broke me,” Choli said gravely. After sometimes twice-daily sessions “they would take me to [a] solitary cell and I would just choke on my blood and drink the blood from inside [my throat],” he said, describing how the feeding tube would scrape him inside. Many of his court records remain sealed and he did not have a lawyer – and medical staff there did not respond to the Guardian’s reporting – so some details in Choli’s account remain uncorroborated.

sentences.en: “It just broke me, mentally broke me,” Choli said gravely.
sentences.zh: “这让我崩溃了，精神上崩溃了，”乔利严肃地说。

sentences.en: After sometimes twice-daily sessions “they would take me to [a] solitary cell and I would just choke on my blood and drink the blood from inside [my throat],” he said, describing how the feeding tube would scrape him inside.
sentences.zh: 有时每天两次的治疗后，“他们会把我带到[一个]单独的牢房，我会因为血液而窒息，然后从[喉咙]里喝血，”他说，并描述了喂食管如何将他刮到里面。

sentences.en: Many of his court records remain sealed and he did not have a lawyer – and medical staff there did not respond to the Guardian’s reporting – so some details in Choli’s account remain uncorroborated.
sentences.zh: 他的许多法庭记录仍然处于密封状态，而且他没有律师，而且那里的医务人员也没有对《卫报》的报道做出回应，因此乔利账户中的一些细节仍未得到证实。

sentences.en: The fence of the Port Isabel detention center.
sentences.zh: 伊莎贝尔港拘留中心的围栏。

sentences.en: Photograph: Verónica G Cárdenas/Reuters
sentences.zh: 摄影：Verónica G Cárdenas/Reuters

blocks.html_en: The Trump administration has not officially acknowledged force-feeding anyone in immigration jails. But an investigation by the Guardian found that since January 2025, the administration used court orders in plans to subject at least 10 hunger strikers in ICE detention to involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding.

sentences.en: The Trump administration has not officially acknowledged force-feeding anyone in immigration jails.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府尚未正式承认对移民监狱中的任何人进行强制喂食。

sentences.en: But an investigation by the Guardian found that since January 2025, the administration used court orders in plans to subject at least 10 hunger strikers in ICE detention to involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding.
sentences.zh: 但《卫报》的一项调查发现，自 2025 年 1 月以来，政府计划利用法院命令对 ICE 拘留中的至少 10 名绝食抗议者进行非自愿医疗程序，包括强制喂食。

blocks.html_en: However, it has since emerged that the number is even higher. Sources with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ICE’s parent agency, later told the Guardian that between January 2025 and 4 August 2026, ICE received “a court order for involuntary treatment for 18 hunger strikers”.

sentences.en: However, it has since emerged that the number is even higher.
sentences.zh: 然而，后来发现这个数字甚至更高。

sentences.en: Sources with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ICE’s parent agency, later told the Guardian that between January 2025 and 4 August 2026, ICE received “a court order for involuntary treatment for 18 hunger strikers”.
sentences.zh: ICE 的上级机构国土安全部 (DHS) 的消息人士后来告诉《卫报》，2025 年 1 月至 2026 年 8 月 4 日期间，ICE 收到“法院命令，对 18 名绝食抗议者进行非自愿治疗”。

blocks.html_en: The DHS did not respond to questions concerning Choli’s specific case, but a spokesperson said in a statement: “ICE respects an individual’s right to refuse medical treatment where appropriate. However, when an individual’s medical condition presents a serious risk of death or permanent harm, or when other compelling legal or operational interests are implicated, ICE may seek judicial authorization for appropriate medical interventions consistent with applicable law.

sentences.en: The DHS did not respond to questions concerning Choli’s specific case, but a spokesperson said in a statement: “ICE respects an individual’s right to refuse medical treatment where appropriate.
sentences.zh: 国土安全部没有回应有关乔利具体案件的问题，但发言人在一份声明中表示：“ICE 尊重个人在适当情况下拒绝医疗的权利。

sentences.en: However, when an individual’s medical condition presents a serious risk of death or permanent harm, or when other compelling legal or operational interests are implicated, ICE may seek judicial authorization for appropriate medical interventions consistent with applicable law.
sentences.zh: 然而，当个人的医疗状况存在严重的死亡或永久伤害风险，或者涉及其他令人信服的法律或运营利益时，ICE 可能会寻求司法授权，以采取符合适用法律的适当医疗干预措施。

blocks.html_en: “Any involuntary medical treatment is undertaken only pursuant to legal authority and under the direction of qualified medical professionals,” the spokesperson added.

sentences.en: “Any involuntary medical treatment is undertaken only pursuant to legal authority and under the direction of qualified medical professionals,” the spokesperson added.
sentences.zh: 发言人补充说：“任何非自愿医疗都只能根据法律授权并在合格的医疗专业人员的指导下进行。”

blocks.html_en: The US attorney’s office in the southern district of Texas did not respond to a detailed request for comment.

sentences.en: The US attorney’s office in the southern district of Texas did not respond to a detailed request for comment.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州南部地区的美国检察官办公室没有回应详细的置评请求。

blocks.html_en: “This likely amounts to torture,” said Dr Chanelle Diaz, an assistant professor of medicine at Columbia University’s medical center, in New York. Diaz has medically evaluated other ICE force-feeding cases and advocated for hunger strikers’ release. She reviewed the limited court records available for Choli’s case, at the Guardian’s request. “I would say that it’s even difficult to capture the degree of risk that he was being put at, long-term,” she said.

sentences.en: “This likely amounts to torture,” said Dr Chanelle Diaz, an assistant professor of medicine at Columbia University’s medical center, in New York.
sentences.zh: “这可能相当于酷刑，”纽约哥伦比亚大学医学中心的医学助理教授夏内尔·迪亚兹博士说。

sentences.en: Diaz has medically evaluated other ICE force-feeding cases and advocated for hunger strikers’ release.
sentences.zh: 迪亚兹对其他 ICE 强制喂食案件进行了医学评估，并主张释放绝食抗议者。

sentences.en: She reviewed the limited court records available for Choli’s case, at the Guardian’s request.
sentences.zh: 应《卫报》的要求，她查阅了有关 Choli 案件的有限法庭记录。

sentences.en: “I would say that it’s even difficult to capture the degree of risk that he was being put at, long-term,” she said.
sentences.zh: “我想说，从长远来看，甚至很难捕捉到他所面临的风险程度，”她说。

blocks.html_en: Choli, a deeply religious Muslim, had been living in Vancouver, where he was a film-maker and activist campaigning for an independent nation of Kurdistan, having come to Canada in 2007 from what he considers occupied territory in Iran. His life was and is complicated. He said he had previously served nine months in prison in Canada following a 2012 drug-smuggling charge and court records show the case was related to receiving just over one kilogram of opium in the mail from Turkey.

sentences.en: Choli, a deeply religious Muslim, had been living in Vancouver, where he was a film-maker and activist campaigning for an independent nation of Kurdistan, having come to Canada in 2007 from what he considers occupied territory in Iran.
sentences.zh: 乔利是一位虔诚的穆斯林，一直住在温哥华，是一名电影制作人和争取库尔德斯坦独立国家的活动家，他于 2007 年从他认为被占领的伊朗领土来到加拿大。

sentences.en: His life was and is complicated.
sentences.zh: 他的生活过去很复杂。

sentences.en: He said he had previously served nine months in prison in Canada following a 2012 drug-smuggling charge and court records show the case was related to receiving just over one kilogram of opium in the mail from Turkey.
sentences.zh: 他表示，2012 年因毒品走私指控，他曾在加拿大监狱服刑 9 个月，法庭记录显示，该案与从土耳其邮寄的略多一公斤的鸦片有关。

blocks.html_en: Then his activism for Kurdish independence drew death threats and in 2022 he crossed the border into the US in Blaine, Washington, and requested asylum. He was quickly released by the authorities and made his way to Los Angeles to try to pursue his ambitions in film while his asylum case played out, attending regular mandatory check-ins with ICE and qualifying for a work permit. Court records say a judge denied his asylum claim in 2024 but granted him protection from deportation to Iran.

sentences.en: Then his activism for Kurdish independence drew death threats and in 2022 he crossed the border into the US in Blaine, Washington, and requested asylum.
sentences.zh: 随后，他的库尔德独立活动引发了死亡威胁，2022 年，他在华盛顿布莱恩越过边境进入美国，并请求庇护。

sentences.en: He was quickly released by the authorities and made his way to Los Angeles to try to pursue his ambitions in film while his asylum case played out, attending regular mandatory check-ins with ICE and qualifying for a work permit.
sentences.zh: 他很快被当局释放，并前往洛杉矶，在他的庇护案件审理期间，试图实现自己的电影抱负，参加 ICE 的定期强制检查并获得工作许可证。

sentences.en: Court records say a judge denied his asylum claim in 2024 but granted him protection from deportation to Iran.
sentences.zh: 法庭记录称，一名法官于 2024 年驳回了他的庇护申请，但给予他保护，免于将他驱逐到伊朗。

blocks.html_en: Then Donald Trump returned to the White House after campaigning on a promise of mass deportation and, at a 25 February 2025 check-in with ICE, Choli was arrested. He was first sent to the Desert View Annex in California, an immigration detention center that has been repeatedly criticized for substandard conditions. While in detention, Choli says he was pressured by ICE officials to sign a deportation order to be sent to Iran. He refused and after demanding better conditions and a fairer resolution to his immigration case, he began his hunger strike on 24 March, court records show.

sentences.en: Then Donald Trump returned to the White House after campaigning on a promise of mass deportation and, at a 25 February 2025 check-in with ICE, Choli was arrested.
sentences.zh: 随后，唐纳德·特朗普在竞选时承诺大规模驱逐出境后返回白宫，并在 2025 年 2 月 25 日向 ICE 报到时，乔利被捕。

sentences.en: He was first sent to the Desert View Annex in California, an immigration detention center that has been repeatedly criticized for substandard conditions.
sentences.zh: 他首先被送往加利福尼亚州的沙漠景观附件，这是一个因条件不合格而多次受到批评的移民拘留中心。

sentences.en: While in detention, Choli says he was pressured by ICE officials to sign a deportation order to be sent to Iran.
sentences.zh: 乔利表示，在被拘留期间，他受到 ICE 官员的压力，要求他签署一份驱逐令，并将其送往伊朗。

sentences.en: He refused and after demanding better conditions and a fairer resolution to his immigration case, he began his hunger strike on 24 March, court records show.
sentences.zh: 法庭记录显示，他拒绝了，在要求为他的移民案提供更好的条件和更公平的解决方案后，他于 3 月 24 日开始绝食。

blocks.html_en: “I am not suicidal,” Choli would later write in a declaration to a federal judge. “I am using hunger strike as the only available option to protest the abuse and mistreatment.”

sentences.en: “I am not suicidal,” Choli would later write in a declaration to a federal judge.
sentences.zh: “我没有自杀倾向，”乔利后来在给联邦法官的一份声明中写道。

sentences.en: “I am using hunger strike as the only available option to protest the abuse and mistreatment.”
sentences.zh: “我将绝食作为抗议虐待和虐待的唯一可用选择。”

blocks.html_en: Choli was then transferred to the privately run Port Isabel facility in Texas for a “higher level of medical care”, an ICE court declaration says. There, Choli refused to end his strike and was placed in a solitary medical cell, which ICE describes as administrative segregation, meaning he was under frequent observation by medical staff. It features a perpetually illuminated cell, alongside other cells in that unit with suicidal or other medically vulnerable detainees.

sentences.en: Choli was then transferred to the privately run Port Isabel facility in Texas for a “higher level of medical care”, an ICE court declaration says.
sentences.zh: ICE 法庭声明称，乔利随后被转移到德克萨斯州伊莎贝尔港的私营机构接受“更高水平的医疗护理”。

sentences.en: There, Choli refused to end his strike and was placed in a solitary medical cell, which ICE describes as administrative segregation, meaning he was under frequent observation by medical staff.
sentences.zh: 在那里，Choli 拒绝结束罢工，并被安置在单独的医疗牢房中，ICE 将其描述为行政隔离，这意味着他经常受到医务人员的观察。

sentences.en: It features a perpetually illuminated cell, alongside other cells in that unit with suicidal or other medically vulnerable detainees.
sentences.zh: 它设有一个永久照明的牢房，以及该牢房内关押有自杀倾向或其他健康状况不佳的被拘留者的其他牢房。

blocks.html_en: Almost 10 days later, ICE sought their first court order to force-feed Choli. He broke his strike, believing the federal court’s involvement could help his immigration case move along. “God opened a door for me,” he said he was thinking, and wrote a letter to the federal judge requesting assistance.

sentences.en: Almost 10 days later, ICE sought their first court order to force-feed Choli.
sentences.zh: 大约 10 天后，ICE 寻求第一份法庭命令，对 Choli 进行强制喂食。

sentences.en: He broke his strike, believing the federal court’s involvement could help his immigration case move along.
sentences.zh: 他打破了罢工，相信联邦法院的参与可以帮助他的移民案件取得进展。

sentences.en: “God opened a door for me,” he said he was thinking, and wrote a letter to the federal judge requesting assistance.
sentences.zh: “上帝为我打开了一扇门，”他说他正在思考，并写了一封信给联邦法官请求帮助。

sentences.en: Kurdish film-maker Gabar Choli photographed in London, Ontario.
sentences.zh: 库尔德电影制片人加巴尔·乔利 (Gabar Choli) 在安大略省伦敦拍摄。

sentences.en: Photograph: Cole Burston/The Guardian
sentences.zh: 摄影：科尔·伯斯顿/卫报

blocks.html_en: But three weeks later, Choli said he learned the case was closed and no one had responded to his letter. Furious, he stopped accepting meals again. On 23 May 2025, ICE and the US attorney’s office for the southern district of Texas filed a second request for a court order to conduct involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding. According to ICE’s request, a social worker at the detention facility evaluated Choli and found he was “operating under his own free will”.

sentences.en: But three weeks later, Choli said he learned the case was closed and no one had responded to his letter.
sentences.zh: 但三周后，乔利表示，他得知案件已经结案，但没有人回复他的信。

sentences.en: Furious, he stopped accepting meals again.
sentences.zh: 他勃然大怒，再次停止吃饭。

sentences.en: On 23 May 2025, ICE and the US attorney’s office for the southern district of Texas filed a second request for a court order to conduct involuntary medical procedures, including force-feeding.
sentences.zh: 2025 年 5 月 23 日，ICE 和美国德克萨斯州南部地区检察官办公室再次请求法院下令实施包括强制喂食在内的非自愿医疗程序。

sentences.en: According to ICE’s request, a social worker at the detention facility evaluated Choli and found he was “operating under his own free will”.
sentences.zh: 根据 ICE 的要求，拘留所的一名社会工作者对 Choli 进行了评估，发现他“是按照自己的自由意志行事”。

blocks.html_en: The World Medical Association and other medical organizations “have said that it is an individual’s right to decide to go on hunger strike, as long as they are of sound mind – which he was”, Dr Parveen Parmar said about Choli after reviewing some of his records shared by the Guardian. Parmar is a doctor and expert with Physicians for Human Rights, a New York-based advocacy group. Like Diaz, she has provided expert medical testimony in other ICE force-feeding cases and also reviewed the limited court records available for Choli’s case.

sentences.en: The World Medical Association and other medical organizations “have said that it is an individual’s right to decide to go on hunger strike, as long as they are of sound mind – which he was”, Dr Parveen Parmar said about Choli after reviewing some of his records shared by the Guardian.
sentences.zh: 世界医学协会和其他医疗组织“曾说过，只要心智健全，个人就有权利决定绝食抗议——他就是这样”，帕文·帕尔玛博士在查看了《卫报》分享的乔利的一些记录后谈到乔利时说道。

sentences.en: Parmar is a doctor and expert with Physicians for Human Rights, a New York-based advocacy group.
sentences.zh: 帕尔玛是一名医生，也是纽约人权医生倡导组织的专家。

sentences.en: Like Diaz, she has provided expert medical testimony in other ICE force-feeding cases and also reviewed the limited court records available for Choli’s case.
sentences.zh: 和迪亚兹一样，她在其他 ICE 强制灌食案件中提供了专家医学证词，并审查了乔利案件的有限法庭记录。

blocks.html_en: “Patient autonomy is one of the core tenets of medicine,” Parmar added.

sentences.en: “Patient autonomy is one of the core tenets of medicine,” Parmar added.
sentences.zh: “患者自主是医学的核心原则之一，”帕尔玛补充道。

blocks.html_en: But as Choli’s hunger strike went on, it threatened his health and also, in the government’s opinion, posed “a serious threat to the security and good order” of the facility, ICE argued in court filings. “The public interest is served by not allowing [Choli’s] attempts to manipulate the immigration system and by maintaining prison and inmate safety and security,” the case documents say.

sentences.en: But as Choli’s hunger strike went on, it threatened his health and also, in the government’s opinion, posed “a serious threat to the security and good order” of the facility, ICE argued in court filings.
sentences.zh: 但 ICE 在法庭文件中辩称，随着乔利的绝食继续，这威胁到了他的健康，而且政府认为，这对设施的“安全和良好秩序构成了严重威胁”。

sentences.en: “The public interest is served by not allowing [Choli’s] attempts to manipulate the immigration system and by maintaining prison and inmate safety and security,” the case documents say.
sentences.zh: 案件文件称：“不允许（乔利）试图操纵移民系统并维护监狱和囚犯的安全，这符合公共利益。”

blocks.html_en: Such filings not only contradict federal silenceor denials about hunger strikes going on intermittently in various ICE detention facilities, but they appear to speak to a desire by authorities to limit such protests from spreading.

sentences.en: Such filings not only contradict federal silenceor denials about hunger strikes going on intermittently in various ICE detention facilities, but they appear to speak to a desire by authorities to limit such protests from spreading.
sentences.zh: 此类文件不仅与联邦消声器否认各 ICE 拘留设施间歇性绝食的说法相矛盾，而且似乎表明当局希望限制此类抗议活动的蔓延。

blocks.html_en: In Choli’s case, doctors working for ICE, Dr Benjamin Salinas and Dr Shauna Kincheloe, also submitted declarations to the court last May requesting the procedures take place – and continue. One day later, the federal judge, Rolando Olvera, ordered Choli to be force-fed, without hearing from Choli himself.

sentences.en: In Choli’s case, doctors working for ICE, Dr Benjamin Salinas and Dr Shauna Kincheloe, also submitted declarations to the court last May requesting the procedures take place – and continue.
sentences.zh: 在 Choli 的案件中，为 ICE 工作的医生 Benjamin Salinas 博士和 Shauna Kincheloe 博士去年 5 月也向法院提交了声明，要求进行并继续进行程序。

sentences.en: One day later, the federal judge, Rolando Olvera, ordered Choli to be force-fed, without hearing from Choli himself.
sentences.zh: 一天后，联邦法官罗兰多·奥尔维拉在没有听取乔利本人的情况下下令对乔利进行强制喂食。

blocks.html_en: When contacted, Salinas told the Guardian: “Thanks for reaching out, but I’m not interested.” Kincheloe did not respond to requests from the Guardian for comment. Olvera’s assistant declined to make the judge available for comment.

sentences.en: When contacted, Salinas told the Guardian: “Thanks for reaching out, but I’m not interested.”
sentences.zh: 当联系上萨利纳斯时，他告诉《卫报》：“感谢您联系我，但我不感兴趣。”

sentences.en: Kincheloe did not respond to requests from the Guardian for comment.
sentences.zh: 金奇洛没有回应《卫报》的置评请求。

sentences.en: Olvera’s assistant declined to make the judge available for comment.
sentences.zh: 奥尔维拉的助手拒绝让法官发表评论。

blocks.html_en: “Immigration detention is civil, it is not necessary,” Diaz said, referring to the fact that many alleged immigration violations, such as remaining in the US without legal status, involve civil, not criminal law. She said that ICE’s court arguments “feel like a false dichotomy”, adding that detained immigrants “could be released, that is always a choice. And that should be the default, not force-feeding.”

sentences.en: “Immigration detention is civil, it is not necessary,” Diaz said, referring to the fact that many alleged immigration violations, such as remaining in the US without legal status, involve civil, not criminal law.
sentences.zh: 迪亚兹说：“移民拘留是民事行为，没有必要。”他指的是许多涉嫌违反移民法的行为，例如在没有合法身份的情况下留在美国，涉及民事法，而不是刑法。

sentences.en: She said that ICE’s court arguments “feel like a false dichotomy”, adding that detained immigrants “could be released, that is always a choice.
sentences.zh: 她表示，ICE 的法庭论点“感觉像是一种错误的二分法”，并补充说被拘留的移民“可以被释放，这始终是一个选择。”

sentences.en: And that should be the default, not force-feeding.”
sentences.zh: 这应该是默认的做法，而不是强制喂食。”

blocks.html_en: In most cases seen by the Guardian, federal judges will often approve ICE’s requests without hearing from the hunger strikers first, or their lawyers – those that have one.

sentences.en: In most cases seen by the Guardian, federal judges will often approve ICE’s requests without hearing from the hunger strikers first, or their lawyers – those that have one.
sentences.zh: 在《卫报》看到的大多数案件中，联邦法官通常会在没有首先听取绝食抗议者或其律师（那些有律师的律师）的意见的情况下批准 ICE 的请求。

blocks.html_en: Choli did not have an attorney during his detention and the entire force-feeding proceedings, records show, and was not provided with one by the government.

sentences.en: Choli did not have an attorney during his detention and the entire force-feeding proceedings, records show, and was not provided with one by the government.
sentences.zh: 记录显示，乔利在被拘留期间和整个强制喂食过程中没有律师，政府也没有提供律师。

blocks.html_en: “In my view, those proceedings shouldn’t continue without the person having legal representation if they don’t have it already,” said Rebecca Sharpless, the founding director of University of Miami’s immigration clinic. Sharpless is not familiar with Choli’s case but represented an ICE hunger striker in 2021 who was ordered force-fed. “It makes a big difference when people understand that there are people who are fighting for them – both in terms of their legal case but also their right to make choices about their body.”

sentences.en: “In my view, those proceedings shouldn’t continue without the person having legal representation if they don’t have it already,” said Rebecca Sharpless, the founding director of University of Miami’s immigration clinic.
sentences.zh: 迈阿密大学移民诊所的创始主任丽贝卡·夏普莱斯 (Rebecca Sharpless) 表示：“在我看来，如果当事人还没有法律代表，那么这些诉讼程序就不应该继续进行。”

sentences.en: Sharpless is not familiar with Choli’s case but represented an ICE hunger striker in 2021 who was ordered force-fed.
sentences.zh: 夏普莱斯并不熟悉 Choli 的案件，但曾在 2021 年代表 ICE 绝食抗议者，该抗议者被下令强制灌食。

sentences.en: “It makes a big difference when people understand that there are people who are fighting for them – both in terms of their legal case but also their right to make choices about their body.”
sentences.zh: “当人们明白有人在为他们而战时，这会带来很大的不同——无论是在法律案件上，还是在他们对自己的身体做出选择的权利方面。”

blocks.html_en: The very first time Choli was force-fed, he had voluntarily gone with the guards to the detention center’s infirmary. But after experiencing the painful and traumatic process for the first time, he began to resist.

sentences.en: The very first time Choli was force-fed, he had voluntarily gone with the guards to the detention center’s infirmary.
sentences.zh: 乔利第一次被灌食时，是自愿跟着恶警去看守所医务室的。

sentences.en: But after experiencing the painful and traumatic process for the first time, he began to resist.
sentences.zh: 但在第一次经历了痛苦和创伤的过程后，他开始反抗。

blocks.html_en: “First I did not resist. But after I saw they were torturing me, I started protesting: ‘I’m not coming with you people,’” he said.

sentences.en: “First I did not resist.
sentences.zh: “首先我没有反抗。

sentences.en: But after I saw they were torturing me, I started protesting: ‘I’m not coming with you people,’” he said.
sentences.zh: 但当我看到他们正在折磨我时，我开始抗议：‘我不会和你们一起去，’”他说。

sentences.en: A security guard poses for a photo next to the group holding cells at Port Isabel.
sentences.zh: 一名保安在伊莎贝尔港的牢房旁拍照。

sentences.en: Photograph: Verónica G Cárdenas/AFP via Getty Images
sentences.zh: 摄影：Verónica G Cárdenas/法新社，盖蒂图片社

blocks.html_en: Then the guards, employees of the private prison company Akima Global Services, “started wrestling”, he said. Many ICE detention centers are run by private US contractors. Akima and its parent company did not respond to detailed requests for comment.

sentences.en: Then the guards, employees of the private prison company Akima Global Services, “started wrestling”, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，然后，私人监狱公司 Akima Global Services 的员工警卫“开始摔跤”。

sentences.en: Many ICE detention centers are run by private US contractors.
sentences.zh: 许多 ICE 拘留中心由美国私人承包商运营。

sentences.en: Akima and its parent company did not respond to detailed requests for comment.
sentences.zh: Akima 及其母公司没有回应详细的置评请求。

blocks.html_en: During the first days of Choli’s force-feeding, his nose and throat were swollen from the repeated tube insertions and removals, according to Choli and court records. He recalled an occasion in which, while being restrained, an ICE nurse “shoved the tube so hard” that “he tore my nose from the inside”. His nose bled for days, Choli wrote in a declaration to the court recounting the incident.

sentences.en: During the first days of Choli’s force-feeding, his nose and throat were swollen from the repeated tube insertions and removals, according to Choli and court records.
sentences.zh: 根据乔利和法庭记录，在乔利强制灌食的最初几天，他的鼻子和喉咙因反复插入和拔除管子而肿胀。

sentences.en: He recalled an occasion in which, while being restrained, an ICE nurse “shoved the tube so hard” that “he tore my nose from the inside”.
sentences.zh: 他回忆起有一次，一名 ICE 护士在受到限制时“用力推管子”，以至于“他从里面撕裂了我的鼻子”。

sentences.en: His nose bled for days, Choli wrote in a declaration to the court recounting the incident.
sentences.zh: 乔利在向法庭陈述事件的一份声明中写道，他的鼻子流血了好几天。

blocks.html_en: Parmar of Physicians for Human Rights said repeated force-feeding can produce such symptoms and is “just inhumane from beginning to end”.

sentences.en: Parmar of Physicians for Human Rights said repeated force-feeding can produce such symptoms and is “just inhumane from beginning to end”.
sentences.zh: 人权医生协会的帕尔玛表示，反复强制喂食会产生此类症状，并且“从头到尾都是不人道的”。

blocks.html_en: The rapid administration of nutrients after Choli had been starving himself also triggered stomach problems. During one early session last June, Choli said he immediately had diarrhea. He was then taken to a cell with no toilet, he said, where he further defecated on himself.

sentences.en: The rapid administration of nutrients after Choli had been starving himself also triggered stomach problems.
sentences.zh: 乔利在挨饿后快速摄入营养物质也引发了胃病。

sentences.en: During one early session last June, Choli said he immediately had diarrhea.
sentences.zh: 在去年六月的一次早期治疗中，乔利说他立即出现腹泻。

sentences.en: He was then taken to a cell with no toilet, he said, where he further defecated on himself.
sentences.zh: 他说，然后他被带到一间没有厕所的牢房，在那里他进一步在身上排便。

blocks.html_en: “I kept looking at my soiled body and clothing and went on crying,” Choli wrote in the declaration to the judge. “I cried for being objectified and inhumanely treated, for seeking a humane treatment.”

sentences.en: “I kept looking at my soiled body and clothing and went on crying,” Choli wrote in the declaration to the judge.
sentences.zh: “我一直看着自己脏兮兮的身体和衣服，不停地哭泣，”乔利在给法官的声明中写道。

sentences.en: “I cried for being objectified and inhumanely treated, for seeking a humane treatment.”
sentences.zh: “我为被物化和非人道对待而哭泣，为寻求人道待遇而哭泣。”

blocks.html_en: Weeks passed and Olvera, the judge, continued to extend the force-feeding order. Choli, with swollen sinuses, presented his declaration to the court at one hearing in mid-June, telling Olvera he could not afford a lawyer and requested a court-appointed attorney.

sentences.en: Weeks passed and Olvera, the judge, continued to extend the force-feeding order.
sentences.zh: 几周过去了，法官奥尔维拉继续延长强制喂食令。

sentences.en: Choli, with swollen sinuses, presented his declaration to the court at one hearing in mid-June, telling Olvera he could not afford a lawyer and requested a court-appointed attorney.
sentences.zh: 鼻窦肿胀的乔利在六月中旬的一次听证会上向法庭提交了声明，告诉奥尔维拉他请不起律师，并要求法庭指定一名律师。

blocks.html_en: Olvera denied Choli’s request, writing in his court order that attorneys are not guaranteed in civil proceedings and that, even if Choli had one, it would be of no use – he would continue to grant force-feeding orders.

sentences.en: Olvera denied Choli’s request, writing in his court order that attorneys are not guaranteed in civil proceedings and that, even if Choli had one, it would be of no use – he would continue to grant force-feeding orders.
sentences.zh: 奥尔维拉拒绝了乔利的请求，并在法庭命令中写道，民事诉讼中没有律师的保障，即使乔利有律师，也没有任何用处——他将继续下达强制喂食令。

blocks.html_en: The twice daily process became a grim routine.

sentences.en: The twice daily process became a grim routine.
sentences.zh: 每天两次的过程变成了残酷的例行公事。

blocks.html_en: Weeks turned to months. At one point, Choli recalled a guard’s rough treatment injuring his ribs, making breathing painful for weeks. At another, guards who were restraining him “pressed so hard on my shoulder, I thought my chest was going to break in half”.

sentences.en: Weeks turned to months.
sentences.zh: 几周变成了几个月。

sentences.en: At one point, Choli recalled a guard’s rough treatment injuring his ribs, making breathing painful for weeks.
sentences.zh: 有一次，乔利回忆起一名警卫的粗暴对待，导致他的肋骨受伤，导致他连续数周呼吸困难。

sentences.en: At another, guards who were restraining him “pressed so hard on my shoulder, I thought my chest was going to break in half”.
sentences.zh: 另一次，控制他的警卫“用力压我的肩膀，我觉得我的胸口要裂成两半”。

blocks.html_en: “I lost my breath” and he heard the doctor say, “‘Take him to the hospital, he’s dead.’ [Then] I completely went ‘out’,” Choli said in an interview.

sentences.en: “I lost my breath” and he heard the doctor say, “‘Take him to the hospital, he’s dead.’ [Then] I completely went ‘out’,” Choli said in an interview.
sentences.zh: “我失去了呼吸”，他听到医生说，“‘带他去医院，他死了。’[然后]我完全‘出去了’，”乔利在接受采访时说。

blocks.html_en: Another time he recalls that despite his warnings a medical staffer incorrectly inserted the tube and it entered his lung, causing him to choke and then cough that end of the tube up into his mouth.

sentences.en: Another time he recalls that despite his warnings a medical staffer incorrectly inserted the tube and it entered his lung, causing him to choke and then cough that end of the tube up into his mouth.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，他回忆道，尽管他提出了警告，一名医务人员还是错误地插入了管子，管子进入了他的肺部，导致他窒息，然后将管子的一端咳到嘴里。

blocks.html_en: Choli remembers that as he was passing out, he “lost [his] senses” and vaguely remembers “reaching for [the guard’s] hand with my mouth”. The DHS, ICE and Akima did not respond to this specific allegation.

sentences.en: Choli remembers that as he was passing out, he “lost [his] senses” and vaguely remembers “reaching for [the guard’s] hand with my mouth”.
sentences.zh: 乔利记得，当他昏倒时，他“失去了知觉”，并模糊地记得“用嘴伸手去抓[警卫]的手”。

sentences.en: The DHS, ICE and Akima did not respond to this specific allegation.
sentences.zh: 国土安全部、ICE 和 Akima 没有对这一具体指控做出回应。

blocks.html_en: Choli said that at one point he made a deal with the facility staff: on Fridays, he agreed to drink the nutritional liquids if they allowed him to pray with other detainees. “That was my opportunity to socialize,” Choli said, calling those Fridays his “peace days”.

sentences.en: Choli said that at one point he made a deal with the facility staff: on Fridays, he agreed to drink the nutritional liquids if they allowed him to pray with other detainees.
sentences.zh: 乔利说，他一度与设施工作人员达成协议：周五，如果他们允许他与其他被拘留者一起祈祷，他同意喝营养液。

sentences.en: “That was my opportunity to socialize,” Choli said, calling those Fridays his “peace days”.
sentences.zh: “那是我社交的机会，”乔利说，他把周五称为“和平日”。

sentences.en: Photograph: Cole Burston/The Guardian
sentences.zh: 摄影：科尔·伯斯顿/卫报

blocks.html_en: Late October rolled around. It was Choli’s birthday and, incredibly, he recalls that Kincheloe, one of the facility doctors, and other nurses sang “Happy Birthday” to him in Spanish. The Guardian has not been able to verify this detail. Choli does not remember whether he drank the nutritional liquids that day or was force-fed.

sentences.en: Late October rolled around.
sentences.zh: 十月下旬转眼就过去了。

sentences.en: It was Choli’s birthday and, incredibly, he recalls that Kincheloe, one of the facility doctors, and other nurses sang “Happy Birthday” to him in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 那天是乔利的生日，令人难以置信的是，他记得金奇洛（该机构的一名医生）和其他护士用西班牙语给他唱了“生日快乐”。

sentences.en: The Guardian has not been able to verify this detail.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》尚未证实这一细节。

sentences.en: Choli does not remember whether he drank the nutritional liquids that day or was force-fed.
sentences.zh: 乔利不记得当天是喝了营养液还是被灌食。

blocks.html_en: “In Choli’s case, where he was force-fed for eight months, you’re looking at easily over 100 NG tube placements, possibly over 200 … that is just not medical care, that is torture,” Diaz said, referring to nasogastric tubing.

sentences.en: “In Choli’s case, where he was force-fed for eight months, you’re looking at easily over 100 NG tube placements, possibly over 200 …
sentences.zh: “在 Choli 的案例中，他被强制灌食了 8 个月，你可以轻松看到 100 多个 NG 管置入，可能超过 200 个……

sentences.en: that is just not medical care, that is torture,” Diaz said, referring to nasogastric tubing.
sentences.zh: “这不是医疗护理，而是酷刑，”迪亚兹说，他指的是鼻胃管。

blocks.html_en: ICE finally deported Choli to Canada on 6 January this year, where he reunited with his siblings who also live in Canada.

sentences.en: ICE finally deported Choli to Canada on 6 January this year, where he reunited with his siblings who also live in Canada.
sentences.zh: ICE 最终于今年 1 月 6 日将 Choli 驱逐到加拿大，在那里他与同样居住在加拿大的兄弟姐妹团聚。

blocks.html_en: He told the Guardian how, the next day, he nervously ate his first solid meal in months, a small, simple salad. He was fine, but his jaw hurt for days.

sentences.en: He told the Guardian how, the next day, he nervously ate his first solid meal in months, a small, simple salad.
sentences.zh: 他告诉《卫报》，第二天，他紧张地吃了几个月来的第一顿固体饭，一份简单的小沙拉。

sentences.en: He was fine, but his jaw hurt for days.
sentences.zh: 他没事，但下巴疼了好几天。

blocks.html_en: “It may sound strange, but I had to learn how to eat [again],” Choli said. He is still struggling today, physically and mentally, but hopes that speaking out may help others in ICE detention.

sentences.en: “It may sound strange, but I had to learn how to eat [again],” Choli said.
sentences.zh: “这可能听起来很奇怪，但我必须（再次）学习如何吃饭，”乔利说。

sentences.en: He is still struggling today, physically and mentally, but hopes that speaking out may help others in ICE detention.
sentences.zh: 如今，他的身体和精神仍在挣扎，但希望发声可以帮助其他被 ICE 拘留的人。

blocks.html_en: “The price of [the hunger strike] was my life,” Choli said in an angry but level and determined tone. “The price of it was my kidneys, my gallbladder. My intestines. My being. My bladder, you know, is damaged. Every time I twist and turn, I feel pain. But this is the price you pay for making a stand for what is right.”

sentences.en: “The price of [the hunger strike] was my life,” Choli said in an angry but level and determined tone.
sentences.zh: “（绝食）的代价就是我的生命，”乔利用愤怒但平静而坚定的语气说道。

sentences.en: “The price of it was my kidneys, my gallbladder.
sentences.zh: “它的代价是我的肾脏、我的胆囊。

sentences.en: My intestines.
sentences.zh: 我的肠子。

sentences.en: My being.
sentences.zh: 我的存在。

sentences.en: My bladder, you know, is damaged.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的膀胱受损了。

sentences.en: Every time I twist and turn, I feel pain.
sentences.zh: 每次我扭动、转动时，我都会感到疼痛。

sentences.en: But this is the price you pay for making a stand for what is right.”
sentences.zh: 但这就是你为坚持正义而付出的代价。”

blocks.html_en: Does he blame Trump?

sentences.en: Does he blame Trump?
sentences.zh: 他责怪特朗普吗？

blocks.html_en: “Trump is just one person,” he said, indicating his problem is with the broader treatment of immigrants and refugees by the US. “Trump is not here torturing me.”

sentences.en: “Trump is just one person,” he said, indicating his problem is with the broader treatment of immigrants and refugees by the US.
sentences.zh: “特朗普只是一个人，”他说，这表明他的问题在于美国对移民和难民的更广泛待遇。

sentences.en: “Trump is not here torturing me.”
sentences.zh: “特朗普不是在这里折磨我。”

blocks.html_en: ICE and the US attorney’s office requested Choli’s force-feeding court case be dismissed in January, saying he was no longer in their custody. An envelope addressed to Choli, containing the dismissal notice, was sent to the Port Isabel detention center. The envelope was returned to the court.

sentences.en: ICE and the US attorney’s office requested Choli’s force-feeding court case be dismissed in January, saying he was no longer in their custody.
sentences.zh: ICE 和美国检察官办公室在一月份要求驳回 Choli 的强制喂食案件，称他已不再被他们拘留。

sentences.en: An envelope addressed to Choli, containing the dismissal notice, was sent to the Port Isabel detention center.
sentences.zh: 一封写给 Choli 的信封内含解雇通知，已被送往伊莎贝尔港拘留中心。

sentences.en: The envelope was returned to the court.
sentences.zh: 信封被退回法庭。

blocks.html_en: “Return to sender”, “Not here,” the envelope read.

sentences.en: “Return to sender”, “Not here,” the envelope read.
sentences.zh: 信封上写着“返回发件人”、“不在这里”。

content_html_zh:
2025年6月，行动迟缓、瘦弱的加巴尔·乔利（Gabar Choli）做好了准备，等待移民拘留中心的警卫再次冲进他的牢房，他的太阳穴凹陷，皮肤下的骨头清晰可见。

乔利被关在伊莎贝尔港服务处理中心内的单独监禁医疗室中，该中心是德克萨斯州南部的移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 拘留设施，唐纳德·特朗普反移民镇压中被捕的移民就被拘留在那里。

40 岁的库尔德寻求庇护者乔利留着浓密的胡须和长长的黑发，他已经绝食两个多月，要求改善被拘留移民的条件并释放或驱逐出境。 他说，2025 年 6 月的那天，乔利的鼻子肿了，喉咙痛，他仍然能尝到前几天接受治疗时的血腥味，而他从未同意过治疗。

这位独立库尔德斯坦的电影制作人和活动人士上周首次发声，他上周在加拿大接受《卫报》独家采访，谈论了他所说的“让他心碎”的美国经历。

他讲述了看守所恶警冲上来，把他按倒在水泥牢房地板上，铐住他的手腕和脚踝，拖到看守所医务室的卑鄙行径。 在那里，恶警将乔利按在床上，医护人员强行将喂食管从他的鼻子插入喉咙，并向他的胃里注入营养液。 Choli 被 ICE 强制灌食。

“两名警卫会抓住我的脚；两名警卫会抓住我的手；一名警卫会抓住我的头——他们会把管子塞进我的鼻子里，”乔利说。 “一天两次被比你更强的男人按倒在地，可不容易。 你只需接受它即可。 你有 60 厘米的管子穿过你，你只能感觉到它的每一厘米。”

《卫报》根据数十页法庭记录以及对医疗和法律专家的采访进行的调查发现，从 2025 年 5 月下旬到 1 月被驱逐出境，Choli 被 ICE 悄悄地、间歇性地强制喂食近八个月。

他并不孤单——他甚至遇到了一位绝食同伴，《卫报》也了解到了一名阿富汗男子，因为他们都在同一个 ICE 设施中被强行喂食。

强制喂食是一个令人痛苦和痛苦的过程，被人权组织广泛谴责为酷刑。 对于乔利和其他人来说，拒绝食物是抗议恶劣条件和移民案件缺乏进展的最后手段，但有时只会带来更恶劣的条件。

“我明白坚持正义的必要性，”乔利在接受《卫报》电话采访时说道，他以一种非常实事求是的方式谈论了他最近的经历。 乔利时常会讽刺地笑起来，现在想起官员们的行为时，他几乎感到难以置信。 “我很尊重。 我只是告诉他们我抗议的是人道待遇，仅此而已。 但他们决心要击溃我，”他说。

根据法庭记录和乔利本人的说法，乔利患有鼻窦肿胀、食道受损、胃病和心理折磨。

“这让我崩溃了，精神上崩溃了，”乔利严肃地说。 有时每天两次的治疗后，“他们会把我带到[一个]单独的牢房，我会因为血液而窒息，然后从[喉咙]里喝血，”他说，并描述了喂食管如何将他刮到里面。 他的许多法庭记录仍然处于密封状态，而且他没有律师，而且那里的医务人员也没有对《卫报》的报道做出回应，因此乔利账户中的一些细节仍未得到证实。

特朗普政府尚未正式承认对移民监狱中的任何人进行强制喂食。 但《卫报》的一项调查发现，自 2025 年 1 月以来，政府计划利用法院命令对 ICE 拘留中的至少 10 名绝食抗议者进行非自愿医疗程序，包括强制喂食。

然而，后来发现这个数字甚至更高。 ICE 的上级机构国土安全部 (DHS) 的消息人士后来告诉《卫报》，2025 年 1 月至 2026 年 8 月 4 日期间，ICE 收到“法院命令，对 18 名绝食抗议者进行非自愿治疗”。

国土安全部没有回应有关乔利具体案件的问题，但发言人在一份声明中表示：“ICE 尊重个人在适当情况下拒绝医疗的权利。 然而，当个人的医疗状况存在严重的死亡或永久伤害风险，或者涉及其他令人信服的法律或运营利益时，ICE 可能会寻求司法授权，以采取符合适用法律的适当医疗干预措施。

发言人补充说：“任何非自愿医疗都只能根据法律授权并在合格的医疗专业人员的指导下进行。”

德克萨斯州南部地区的美国检察官办公室没有回应详细的置评请求。

“这可能相当于酷刑，”纽约哥伦比亚大学医学中心的医学助理教授夏内尔·迪亚兹博士说。 迪亚兹对其他 ICE 强制喂食案件进行了医学评估，并主张释放绝食抗议者。 应《卫报》的要求，她查阅了有关 Choli 案件的有限法庭记录。 “我想说，从长远来看，甚至很难捕捉到他所面临的风险程度，”她说。

乔利是一位虔诚的穆斯林，一直住在温哥华，是一名电影制作人和争取库尔德斯坦独立国家的活动家，他于 2007 年从他认为被占领的伊朗领土来到加拿大。 他的生活过去很复杂。 他表示，2012 年因毒品走私指控，他曾在加拿大监狱服刑 9 个月，法庭记录显示，该案与从土耳其邮寄的略多一公斤的鸦片有关。

随后，他的库尔德独立活动引发了死亡威胁，2022 年，他在华盛顿布莱恩越过边境进入美国，并请求庇护。 他很快被当局释放，并前往洛杉矶，在他的庇护案件审理期间，试图实现自己的电影抱负，参加 ICE 的定期强制检查并获得工作许可证。 法庭记录称，一名法官于 2024 年驳回了他的庇护申请，但给予他保护，免于将他驱逐到伊朗。

随后，唐纳德·特朗普在竞选时承诺大规模驱逐出境后返回白宫，并在 2025 年 2 月 25 日向 ICE 报到时，乔利被捕。 他首先被送往加利福尼亚州的沙漠景观附件，这是一个因条件不合格而多次受到批评的移民拘留中心。 乔利表示，在被拘留期间，他受到 ICE 官员的压力，要求他签署一份驱逐令，并将其送往伊朗。 法庭记录显示，他拒绝了，在要求为他的移民案提供更好的条件和更公平的解决方案后，他于 3 月 24 日开始绝食。

“我没有自杀倾向，”乔利后来在给联邦法官的一份声明中写道。 “我将绝食作为抗议虐待和虐待的唯一可用选择。”

ICE 法庭声明称，乔利随后被转移到德克萨斯州伊莎贝尔港的私营机构接受“更高水平的医疗护理”。 在那里，Choli 拒绝结束罢工，并被安置在单独的医疗牢房中，ICE 将其描述为行政隔离，这意味着他经常受到医务人员的观察。 它设有一个永久照明的牢房，以及该牢房内关押有自杀倾向或其他健康状况不佳的被拘留者的其他牢房。

大约 10 天后，ICE 寻求第一份法庭命令，对 Choli 进行强制喂食。 他打破了罢工，相信联邦法院的参与可以帮助他的移民案件取得进展。 “上帝为我打开了一扇门，”他说他正在思考，并写了一封信给联邦法官请求帮助。

但三周后，乔利表示，他得知案件已经结案，但没有人回复他的信。 他勃然大怒，再次停止吃饭。 2025 年 5 月 23 日，ICE 和美国德克萨斯州南部地区检察官办公室再次请求法院下令实施包括强制喂食在内的非自愿医疗程序。 根据 ICE 的要求，拘留所的一名社会工作者对 Choli 进行了评估，发现他“是按照自己的自由意志行事”。

世界医学协会和其他医疗组织“曾说过，只要心智健全，个人就有权利决定绝食抗议——他就是这样”，帕文·帕尔玛博士在查看了《卫报》分享的乔利的一些记录后谈到乔利时说道。 帕尔玛是一名医生，也是纽约人权医生倡导组织的专家。 和迪亚兹一样，她在其他 ICE 强制灌食案件中提供了专家医学证词，并审查了乔利案件的有限法庭记录。

“患者自主是医学的核心原则之一，”帕尔玛补充道。

但 ICE 在法庭文件中辩称，随着乔利的绝食继续，这威胁到了他的健康，而且政府认为，这对设施的“安全和良好秩序构成了严重威胁”。 案件文件称：“不允许（乔利）试图操纵移民系统并维护监狱和囚犯的安全，这符合公共利益。”

此类文件不仅与联邦消声器否认各 ICE 拘留设施间歇性绝食的说法相矛盾，而且似乎表明当局希望限制此类抗议活动的蔓延。

在 Choli 的案件中，为 ICE 工作的医生 Benjamin Salinas 博士和 Shauna Kincheloe 博士去年 5 月也向法院提交了声明，要求进行并继续进行程序。 一天后，联邦法官罗兰多·奥尔维拉在没有听取乔利本人的情况下下令对乔利进行强制喂食。

当联系上萨利纳斯时，他告诉《卫报》：“感谢您联系我，但我不感兴趣。” 金奇洛没有回应《卫报》的置评请求。 奥尔维拉的助手拒绝让法官发表评论。

迪亚兹说：“移民拘留是民事行为，没有必要。”他指的是许多涉嫌违反移民法的行为，例如在没有合法身份的情况下留在美国，涉及民事法，而不是刑法。 她表示，ICE 的法庭论点“感觉像是一种错误的二分法”，并补充说被拘留的移民“可以被释放，这始终是一个选择。” 这应该是默认的做法，而不是强制喂食。”

在《卫报》看到的大多数案件中，联邦法官通常会在没有首先听取绝食抗议者或其律师（那些有律师的律师）的意见的情况下批准 ICE 的请求。

记录显示，乔利在被拘留期间和整个强制喂食过程中没有律师，政府也没有提供律师。

迈阿密大学移民诊所的创始主任丽贝卡·夏普莱斯 (Rebecca Sharpless) 表示：“在我看来，如果当事人还没有法律代表，那么这些诉讼程序就不应该继续进行。” 夏普莱斯并不熟悉 Choli 的案件，但曾在 2021 年代表 ICE 绝食抗议者，该抗议者被下令强制灌食。 “当人们明白有人在为他们而战时，这会带来很大的不同——无论是在法律案件上，还是在他们对自己的身体做出选择的权利方面。”

乔利第一次被灌食时，是自愿跟着恶警去看守所医务室的。 但在第一次经历了痛苦和创伤的过程后，他开始反抗。

“首先我没有反抗。 但当我看到他们正在折磨我时，我开始抗议：‘我不会和你们一起去，’”他说。

他说，然后，私人监狱公司 Akima Global Services 的员工警卫“开始摔跤”。 许多 ICE 拘留中心由美国私人承包商运营。 Akima 及其母公司没有回应详细的置评请求。

根据乔利和法庭记录，在乔利强制灌食的最初几天，他的鼻子和喉咙因反复插入和拔除管子而肿胀。 他回忆起有一次，一名 ICE 护士在受到限制时“用力推管子”，以至于“他从里面撕裂了我的鼻子”。 乔利在向法庭陈述事件的一份声明中写道，他的鼻子流血了好几天。

人权医生协会的帕尔玛表示，反复强制喂食会产生此类症状，并且“从头到尾都是不人道的”。

乔利在挨饿后快速摄入营养物质也引发了胃病。 在去年六月的一次早期治疗中，乔利说他立即出现腹泻。 他说，然后他被带到一间没有厕所的牢房，在那里他进一步在身上排便。

“我一直看着自己脏兮兮的身体和衣服，不停地哭泣，”乔利在给法官的声明中写道。 “我为被物化和非人道对待而哭泣，为寻求人道待遇而哭泣。”

几周过去了，法官奥尔维拉继续延长强制喂食令。 鼻窦肿胀的乔利在六月中旬的一次听证会上向法庭提交了声明，告诉奥尔维拉他请不起律师，并要求法庭指定一名律师。

奥尔维拉拒绝了乔利的请求，并在法庭命令中写道，民事诉讼中没有律师的保障，即使乔利有律师，也没有任何用处——他将继续下达强制喂食令。

每天两次的过程变成了残酷的例行公事。

几周变成了几个月。 有一次，乔利回忆起一名警卫的粗暴对待，导致他的肋骨受伤，导致他连续数周呼吸困难。 另一次，控制他的警卫“用力压我的肩膀，我觉得我的胸口要裂成两半”。

“我失去了呼吸”，他听到医生说，“‘带他去医院，他死了。’[然后]我完全‘出去了’，”乔利在接受采访时说。

还有一次，他回忆道，尽管他提出了警告，一名医务人员还是错误地插入了管子，管子进入了他的肺部，导致他窒息，然后将管子的一端咳到嘴里。

乔利记得，当他昏倒时，他“失去了知觉”，并模糊地记得“用嘴伸手去抓[警卫]的手”。 国土安全部、ICE 和 Akima 没有对这一具体指控做出回应。

乔利说，他一度与设施工作人员达成协议：周五，如果他们允许他与其他被拘留者一起祈祷，他同意喝营养液。 “那是我社交的机会，”乔利说，他把周五称为“和平日”。

十月下旬转眼就过去了。 那天是乔利的生日，令人难以置信的是，他记得金奇洛（该机构的一名医生）和其他护士用西班牙语给他唱了“生日快乐”。 《卫报》尚未证实这一细节。 乔利不记得当天是喝了营养液还是被灌食。

“在 Choli 的案例中，他被强制灌食了 8 个月，你可以轻松看到 100 多个 NG 管置入，可能超过 200 个…… “这不是医疗护理，而是酷刑，”迪亚兹说，他指的是鼻胃管。

ICE 最终于今年 1 月 6 日将 Choli 驱逐到加拿大，在那里他与同样居住在加拿大的兄弟姐妹团聚。

他告诉《卫报》，第二天，他紧张地吃了几个月来的第一顿固体饭，一份简单的小沙拉。 他没事，但下巴疼了好几天。

“这可能听起来很奇怪，但我必须（再次）学习如何吃饭，”乔利说。 如今，他的身体和精神仍在挣扎，但希望发声可以帮助其他被 ICE 拘留的人。

“（绝食）的代价就是我的生命，”乔利用愤怒但平静而坚定的语气说道。 “它的代价是我的肾脏、我的胆囊。 我的肠子。 我的存在。 你知道，我的膀胱受损了。 每次我扭动、转动时，我都会感到疼痛。 但这就是你为坚持正义而付出的代价。”

他责怪特朗普吗？

“特朗普只是一个人，”他说，这表明他的问题在于美国对移民和难民的更广泛待遇。 “特朗普不是在这里折磨我。”

ICE 和美国检察官办公室在一月份要求驳回 Choli 的强制喂食案件，称他已不再被他们拘留。 一封写给 Choli 的信封内含解雇通知，已被送往伊莎贝尔港拘留中心。 信封被退回法庭。

信封上写着“返回发件人”、“不在这里”。
